key_themes: Fed hawkish shock: Warsh's first FOMC leaves rates at 3.5-3.75% but dot plot surges to 3.8% median, signaling late-2026 rate hike
SpaceX (SPCX) post-IPO volatility: shares reverse gains, falling ~5% as macro headwinds hit newly-public meme-stock darling
Chemicals sector M&A: Huntsman + Olin announce $12B+ all-stock merger of equals to form OlinHuntsman Corp

stocks.discussion_driver: SpaceX debuted June 12 at $135 in the largest IPO ever, surging to an intraday ATH of $225.64 before falling ~5% on June 17 as hawkish Fed signals dampened meme-stock momentum. With only a small retail float relative to its ~$1.9T+ implied valuation, price discovery is nascent and highly sentiment-driven.
bull_case: Starlink and Starship revenue potential creates a multi-trillion dollar long-term growth story in commercial space and satellite internet
Largest IPO in history reflects massive institutional and retail demand, validating the commercial space economy at scale
bear_case: Former Nasdaq chief warns SPCX is not trading on fundamentals; meme-stock momentum can unwind sharply with the limited public float amplifying downside volatility
Fed hawkish shock and bond yield spike directly pressure speculative-growth premiums; macro headwinds could deflate the sentiment-driven valuation

stocks.discussion_driver: La-Z-Boy delivered a standout Q4 FY2026 with EPS of $1.26 — 54% above the $0.82 consensus — and announced a $300M share buyback program. Shares surged ~17.7% after hours, pushing the stock to a new 52-week high as management signaled confidence through accelerating capital return.
bull_case: Q4 FY2026 EPS of $1.26 crushed $0.82 consensus (+54%), demonstrating strong operational execution and demand resilience in home furnishings
$300M buyback authorization plus a history of 10% annual dividend growth signal management confidence and provide meaningful shareholder return support
bear_case: Consumer discretionary weakness from a hawkish Fed and elevated rates could pressure big-ticket furniture purchases into FY2027
Thin analyst coverage (only 2 analysts) limits institutional price discovery and leaves the stock vulnerable to sharp moves on any guidance change

stocks.discussion_driver: CarMax beat Q1 FY2027 estimates soundly — EPS $1.31 vs. $0.96 est. (+36%), revenue up 6.2% to $8.0B — but shares declined ~2.4% premarket as investors processed cautious commentary on used-vehicle margins and price normalization. The stock trades at a significant premium to analyst targets despite bottom-of-cycle dynamics in auto retail.
bull_case: Q1 FY2027 EPS of $1.31 beat the $0.96 consensus by 36%, with total unit sales up 3.3% YoY and wholesale units surging 8.4%, demonstrating resilient volume
CarMax Auto Finance (CAF) is emerging as a high-margin growth driver, successfully expanding into the broader credit spectrum beyond prime borrowers
bear_case: Wall Street consensus price target of $42.15 sits ~18% below the current $51.30, with Barclays maintaining Underweight at $31 — institutional skepticism on valuation is significant
Trailing PE of 32.2x is well above the 5-year median of 20.6x; ongoing margin pressure from used-vehicle price normalization and profit-dilutive price cuts are structural headwinds

stocks.discussion_driver: Shares surged ~75% after the FDA agreed with uniQure's plan to file a BLA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, targeting Q3 2026 submission for accelerated approval review. This Type B meeting outcome removes the biggest binary regulatory risk and is a major de-risking event for the only gene therapy program in late-stage development for HD.
bull_case: FDA acceptance of the BLA filing pathway for AMT-130 removes the primary regulatory binary risk and opens a clear route to accelerated approval for the first Huntington's disease gene therapy
Q3 2026 BLA submission timeline established; accelerated approval could enable commercial launch within 12-18 months, with no currently approved HD treatments on market
bear_case: Clinical-stage biotech with no revenues and high cash burn — remains dependent on capital markets with a negative earnings profile until potential commercialization
Huntington's disease affects approximately 30,000 US patients, creating a narrow commercial ceiling; current analyst price targets (~$45 avg) are now below the post-surge price of $47.67

stocks.discussion_driver: Huntsman fell ~18% on June 17 after announcing an all-stock merger with Olin Corp to form OlinHuntsman Corporation. The 0.5476 Olin shares per HUN exchange ratio implied a value of ~$13 — well below HUN's June 16 close of $15.89 — triggering aggressive merger-arb selling as the deal effectively priced Huntsman at a discount to its prior trading price.
bull_case: The OlinHuntsman merger creates a $12.5B integrated North American chemicals leader with $400M+ in expected cost synergies, improving competitive position from a deep industry trough
Mizuho upgraded HUN to Neutral from Underperform on the deal announcement, signaling analyst sentiment may be inflecting from a prior bearish consensus
bear_case: The merger exchange ratio valued HUN at a discount to its pre-announcement close — Huntsman shareholders effectively received no acquisition premium and gave away upside to Olin holders
Transaction not expected to close until H1 2027, creating 12 months of deal-risk limbo, regulatory review uncertainty, and continued chemical-cycle macro exposure
